notes.1: Makes 1 large braided loaf, about 12 slices.

move.title: Mastery: a cardamom braid
move.body: Pulla is the cardamom bread Finnish families bake for coffee time, braided and shiny with egg wash and pearl sugar. This is the unit's mastery week, so you bake it on your own: an enriched dough kneaded to a windowpane, three ropes weighed to match, a tight braid, and a loaf you check by its color, its sound, and 190°F in the center.

callback.body: Pita is a lean dough that rises in an hour. Pulla adds milk, butter, egg, and sugar, so it rises slower and bakes soft and golden, and it's rolled into ropes and braided instead of rolled flat.

why.title: A rich dough rises slowly
why.body: Milk, butter, egg, and sugar make pulla soft and sweet, but fat coats the gluten and sugar pulls water from the yeast. Give it the full rise, even when it seems slow.

why.title: The windowpane test
why.body: A braid stretches its ropes. When a small piece of dough stretches thin enough to see light through, the gluten can stretch without tearing.

why.title: Ropes that match
why.body: Three ropes within a tenth of an ounce of each other braid into an even loaf. A heavier rope pulls the braid toward it and stays doughy while the others brown.

why.title: Egg wash and pearl sugar
why.body: Egg brushed on before baking browns deeply and shines. It's also the glue that holds the pearl sugar, which doesn't melt in the oven and stays white and crunchy.

why.title: Three checks
why.body: Egg wash and sugar brown the crust early, so color isn't enough. The bottom should sound hollow when tapped, and the center should read 190°F.

wrong.sign: A rope keeps shrinking back as you roll it
wrong.fix: Leave it under the towel 5 minutes, then roll it again.

wrong.sign: The braid leans or curves to one side
wrong.fix: The ropes weren't the same weight. Weigh them next time, and keep the plait snug and even.

wrong.sign: The loaf split open along one side
wrong.fix: It wasn't proofed long enough. Wait until a gentle poke springs back slowly.

wrong.sign: The top is deep brown but the center reads under 190°F
wrong.fix: Lay foil loosely over the top and bake 5 more minutes.

quiz.q: What warm milk temperature wakes up the yeast?
quiz.explain: Above about 130°F starts to kill it.

choices: So the braid bakes evenly and sits straight
quiz.explain: A heavy rope stays doughy and pulls the braid.

quiz.q: What holds the pearl sugar on?
quiz.explain: Egg wash glues it and browns the crust.

choices: Golden, hollow-sounding, and 190°F in the center
quiz.explain: The crust browns before the middle is set.

ingredients.text: a little more, for the bowl

substitutions.note: Pearl sugar is sold in the baking aisle of some stores and online. Or crush 8 sugar cubes into small chunks, or sprinkle 1 tablespoon of sugar.

steps.text: Warm the cup of milk in the measuring cup in the microwave for about 40 seconds. Stir and check it with the thermometer: 105 to 110°F.
Pour the milk into the large bowl. Stir in 1 teaspoon of the sugar, sprinkle the yeast over the top, and leave it to bloom.
steps.look: Foam on top, and it smells like bread.

steps.text: Add the rest of the sugar, the dough's egg, the cardamom, and the salt, and beat with the fork.
Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshell.
Stir in 3½ cups of the flour with the wooden spoon, then the softened butter, then as much of the last ½ cup as it takes to make a soft, sticky dough.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw dough. It has raw egg and raw flour.

steps.text: Turn the dough onto a lightly floured counter. Knead until it's smooth and passes the windowpane test. If it tears, knead 2 more minutes and test again.
steps.look: Smooth and soft, and a small piece stretches thin enough to see light through.

steps.text: Butter the bowl, put the dough in, and turn it once to coat it. Cover with the towel and leave it somewhere warm until it doubles.
steps.look: Doubled. A floured finger pressed in leaves a dent that stays.

steps.text: Line the sheet pan with parchment. Weigh the dough and divide the weight by 3. Cut 3 pieces, weighing each, and pinch dough from heavy pieces onto light ones until they're within a tenth of an ounce. Roll each into a rope 18 inches long, a little thicker in the middle.
steps.look: Three ropes the same length, each tapered the same way.

steps.text: Pinch the ropes together at the top and braid them, outside rope over the middle, left then right, snug but not stretched. Pinch the bottom ends together, tuck both ends under, and lift the braid onto the pan.
Cover the loaf loosely with the towel and let it proof. Heat the oven to 375°F while it does.
steps.look: Puffy, about half again as big. A gentle poke springs back slowly and leaves a small dent.

steps.text: Beat the last egg with the tablespoon of milk in the small bowl. Brush it over the braid and into its folds, and sprinkle the pearl sugar over the top.
Wash your hands and the brush with soap, and throw away the rest of the egg wash.
Bake the pulla. Check it at 15 minutes, and if the top is already deep brown, lay a sheet of foil loosely over it.
steps.look: Deep golden and shiny, with white pearl sugar.

steps.text: With oven mitts, pull the pan out partway. Push the thermometer into the thickest part from the side: 190°F. Tip the loaf up with a mitt and tap the bottom: it should sound hollow. If either check fails, bake 5 more minutes and check again.
Turn off the oven. Slide the pulla onto the cooling rack and let it cool before slicing.
